chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Harun, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, raising it, said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who engage in mutual sodomy. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The penalty (hadd) for both of them is the penalty (hadd) of the adulterer. So if one of them is the active partner upon his companion, the active one is struck with one strike with the sword, which takes from him what it takes and leaves from him what it leaves, intending his death by it; and the passive one is burnt in the fire.'

key_terms.الدَّاعِمُ: the active partner (the one who exerts force)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific hadd penalty for the active and passive partners in male sodomy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific hadd penalties for male homosexual intercourse, distinguishing between the active partner (al-da'im), who is executed by the sword, and the passive partner, who is burned with fire. The description of the sword strike as one that 'takes what it takes and leaves what it leaves' reflects the classical juristic interpretation of a decisive, fatal blow, while the burning of the passive partner highlights the severity of the act in Shia legal tradition.
